# m.reference.ticker_events

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The timeline of a ticker's events, such as ticker changes, one row per event.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.reference.ticker_events(symbols, *, types=None)
```

- [Query methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol`, `Date` and `Type`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows the [shared rules](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Tickers of any classes (`dm.ALL` is refused). |
| `types` | The event types to include, such as `["ticker_change"]` (one `str` is one type); None for every type. |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Ticker Events (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks Basic | Updated daily, 2 years |
| Stocks Starter | Updated daily, All history |
| Stocks Developer | Updated daily, All history |
| Stocks Advanced | Updated daily, All history |
| Stocks Business | Updated daily, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST: the request's `id` parameter. |
| `Date` | String | The date the event took place |
| `Type` | String | The type of historical event for the asset |
| `TickerChangeTicker` | String | A ticker symbol. From the `ticker_change` object: Details about a ticker change. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. |
